newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong robbers take flight with chicken wings.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong robbers take flight with chicken wings.

text.p: In a rich city more often plagued by gold, jewelry and bank heists, robbers have found a novel precious commodity to rob -- chicken wings.

Robbers boarded a container barge on Sunday night, tied up, gagged and blindfolded the watchman, and escaped with five containers full of imported frozen chicken wings worth HK$2.5 million ($323,400), Hong Kong radio said.
About six men boarded the barge carrying the refrigerated containers and transferred them to another boat, the radio said.
Poultry -- especially chicken wings and feet -- is a commodity in hot demand with Chinese consumers. Vast quantities are imported annually for Hong Kong and China dining tables.
China is the second largest market for U.S. poultry products after Russia, and it is the only market for chicken feet.
Chicken wings and chicken feet are considered a delicacy in Chinese cuisine.
